figures.title: Proactive vs. reactive AI agents
figures.alt: Reactive agents wait for explicit requests; proactive agents use awareness, anticipation, agenda formation, arbitration, action, and adaptation.

figures.title: Proactiveness as delegated residual discretion
figures.alt: A task execution space divided into explicit task instructions and a residual decision space: preference and trade-off decisions, procedural underspecification, contingency and risk underspecification, and adaptive replanning.

figures.title: From complementary capabilities to earned autonomy
figures.alt: Intelligence, alignment, and proactiveness build trust, which enables greater delegated autonomy.

figures.title: The reactivity-proactivity spectrum
figures.alt: A progression from reactive response to mixed-initiative assistance and self-initiated agency, as the human's role moves from operator to collaborator to reviewer.

figures.title: Historical foundations of increasingly open-ended initiative
figures.alt: A timeline from control and cybernetics through planning, agent theory, ubiquitous computing, mixed initiative, goal reasoning, and foundation-model agents.

figures.title: Six interacting capacities for exercising proactive discretion
figures.alt: Awareness, anticipation, agenda, arbitration, and action form a cycle; adaptation sits at the center and feeds back into each of them.

figures.title: Awareness grounds initiative in decision-relevant context
figures.alt: Awareness combines multimodal state tracking, active information seeking, hierarchical memory, and runtime architectures.

figures.title: Anticipation establishes why an intervention may be worth initiating
figures.alt: Anticipation models the user and world, compares acting with abstaining, and rehearses possible scenarios.

figures.title: Agenda bridges foresight and sustained goal pursuit
figures.alt: Agenda formation moves from goal generation through sub-goal proposal and standing agenda to conflict resolution and selection.

figures.title: Arbitration: a worthwhile goal is not yet a warranted intervention
figures.alt: An arbitration gate tests confidence, value versus cost, timing, and risk and reversibility before licensing intervention.

figures.title: Action: exercising discretion while preserving human control
figures.alt: An action pipeline covers selection, delivery, and guardrails and recovery, with initiative ranging from reactive to proactive.

figures.title: Adaptation: learning whether initiative was warranted
figures.alt: User and environment responses feed fast reflection and slow calibration back into the proactive agent's capacities.

figures.title: Evaluating proactiveness requires evidence beyond task completion
figures.alt: Evaluation spans task utility, mechanism-level evaluation, and user experience.

figures.title: From executing assigned tasks to sustaining delegated objectives
figures.alt: Across agent categories, higher proactiveness and authority move agents from executing an assigned task to working through awareness, anticipation, agenda, arbitration, action, and adaptation.

figures.title: Three cross-industry trends in proactive AI
figures.alt: Applications move from foundation models to long-horizon tasks, while improvement depends on evaluation and feedback infrastructure.
